Title: Change Length
Content: Objective Type in the segment length and edit Pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the segment to be adjusted to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Change Length. The Change Length window appears. Enter the length of the segment and select the desired location. The preview shows in the 2D window. Click OK. The segment length is changed accordingly. Note: If a line connected to the selected line is a curve, the curve point is moved according to the changed length. If the "Lock Curve Points" option is checked, only straight points can be moved. (ver MD10)

Title: Cut/ Cut & Sew
Content: Objective Cut a single 2D Pattern into two or more pieces using Internal Lines (ver2.3.0). Location Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Trace Tool (ver2.4.0) Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Operation Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut &amp Sew. The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut &amp Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. Trace Tool Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Trace 2D Toolbar Trace Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut &amp Sew. The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut &amp Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. Note: With the Trace tool, you can Cut or Cut &amp Sew Patterns using the Baselines as well.

Title: Clone as Pattern/Internal Shape
Content: Objective Duplicate an Internal Shape as an identical shaped Pattern or vice-versa. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern (A)/ Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Operation Clone as Pattern (ver2.4.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern (A)/ Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Right click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated as a Pattern to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Clone as Pattern. The duplicated Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D window to place the Pattern. Clone as Pattern (With Sewing) (ver. 12.2) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern (A) / Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Right click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated as a Pattern to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Clone as Pattern (With Sewing). The duplicated Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. Sewing lines are automatically generated between the selected Internal Shape and the duplicated Pattern, except in the following cases * Where a Segment does not have angle between its first and last points. (Where two points are on a straight line) * Where the selected segments are not connected to each other. Click on the 2D window to place the pattern. Clone as Internal Shape Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern (A)/ Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Right click on the Pattern to be duplicated as an Internal Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Clone as Internal Shape. The duplicated Internal Shape follows along the mouse cursor. Click on the desired Pattern to place the Internal Shape. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard while pasting the duplicated Pattern/Internal Shape to move it on a straight line or on a diagonal line.

Title: Layer Clone
Content: Objective Create an instance of the Pattern in its 3D state while sewing its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to its instance's Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. Use the function to easily create padded jackets, collars, cuffs and other garments/details made with multiple layers of Patterns. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu Layer Clone (Over/Under) Operation Select Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. Select the Patterns to be layer cloned. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu Layer Clone (Over) The cloned Pattern is placed above the original Pattern. Right Click Pop-Up Menu Layer Clone (Under) The cloned Pattern is placed beneath the original Pattern. Activate Simulation. The cloned layer is simulated based on the option selected.

Title: Linked Editing
Content: Objective Copy and paste/mirror paste Patterns with Linked Editing function to edit them simultaneously. Or apply linked editing function to existing pair of symmetric Patterns (ver3.0.0). Location Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern Apply Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Apply Linked Editing Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern Remove Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Remove Linked Editing Operation Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Select the Pattern to be duplicated with the Transform Pattern tool. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern The clone of the Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. Symmetric Patterns's outline is highlighted in light-blue (ver2.5.0). Click on the 2D window to place the clone. The selected Pattern is pasted/mirror pasted with Linked Editing function. Note: When copying the Pattern as an instance (Instance Pattern,) right click on the 2D window to access the Paste window which allows you to set Interval and Number of Shapes. Apply Linked Editing Select the patterns to be linked with the Transform Pattern tool. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Apply Linked Editing Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern Selected Patterns are linked and can be edited simultaneously. Remove Linked Editing Select the Patterns which the Linked Editing function should be removed with the Transform Pattern tool. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Remove Linked Editing The applied Linked Editing function is removed.

Title: Mirror Paste
Content: Objective Mirror Paste copied Pattern/Internal Shape. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) Mirror Paste (Ctrl + R) Operation Navigate to 2D toolbar and select Transform Pattern Tool or Edit Pattern Tool. Then, copy the desired Pattern or Internal Shape. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) Mirror Paste (Ctrl + R) The clone of copied Pattern/Internal Shape follows along the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D window or on the Pattern to place the Pattern or the Internal Shape. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to move the duplicated Pattern on a straight line or on a diagonal line. Select the desired Pattern and hit Ctrl + C (Copy) / Ctrl +V(Paste), Ctrl + R(Mirror Paste) on the keyboard to copy and paste Patterns to a separate CLO window (ver3.0.0).

Title: Offset as Internal Line
Content: Objective Input specific measurements to offset Patterns and segments as Internal Lines. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern Operation Offset as Internal Line Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern Right click on top of a Pattern and select Offset As Internal Line from the pop-up menu. The Offset as Internal Line window appears. Configure the settings as needed. Distance Set the interval between each Internal Line. Number of Lines Set the number of Internal Lines to be generated (ver2.4.0) Reverse Direction Offset the Internal Lines in the opposite direction. Extend Automatically extend the Internal Lines to the perimeter of the Pattern. Click OK. The offset Internal Lines appear in the 2D window. Offset as Internal Line along Curve (ver3.2.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern Select the two Pattern outlines between where the Internal Lines are created. Right click on the selected Pattern outline and select Offset as Internal Line along Curve. The Distribute Internal Line between Segment window appears. Adjust the options below as needed, then select OK. Name Description Number of Offsets Set the number of Internal Lines to be created. Offset Set the distance between each Internal Lines. Distance to Segment Edge Set the distance from the Pattern outlines for the Internal Lines. - Reverse Direction Horizontally reverse the Internal Lines' position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. - Opposite Segment Vertically reverse the Internal Lines' position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. Straight Create Internal Lines as straight lines. Perpendicular Direction Create Internal Lines perpendicular to the selected Pattern outlines. Internal Lines are created based on the above settings. Note: Using the same function, additional Internal Lines can be created between Internal Lines. When the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines are divided in multiple segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to select them all.

Title: Copy/Paste
Content: Objective Copy and Paste Patterns as needed. Location 2D Tool Bar Transform Pattern Tool or Edit Pattern Tool Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern or Internal Line) Copy (Ctrl+C) or Paste (Ctrl+V) Clone of the Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. Clone on the desired position within the 2D window to place the clone. The Pattern and Internal Line are copied to the clicked point. Note: When pasting, hold down the Shift key to place a Pattern on the vertical/horizontal/45 line. Patterns can be copied and pasted even between multiple executed programs. When pasting, Right Click to enter Interval/Number of Shapes/Position(Internal Line) values. A part of internal shapes can be copied and paste. (ver MD10)

Title: Delete All Overlapping Points
Content: Objective Delete overlapping points on patterns/internal shapes (ver2.5.0). When cutting Patterns in Marvelous Designer, two Segment Points can be created very close to each other, below the minimum distance set by Marvelous Designer. When the aforementioned case happens, the respective Patterns cannot be moved nor edited, but can be resolved by deleting the overlapping points. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) Delete All Overlapping Points Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) Delete All Overlapping Points All overlapping points on Patterns and Internal Shapes are deleted.

Title: Transform Point/Segment
Content: Objective Transform a Pattern by scaling or rotating its point and segment. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button) Transform Point/Segment Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button) Transform Point/Segment Select the point/segment to be transformed. The selected point/segment is highlighted in yellow and the surrounding marquee box appears. The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) Move, scale, or rotate the selected point/segment. The Pattern is transformed as the selected points/segments are edited.

Title: Polygon Lasso Selection
Content: Objective Select Patterns, Sewing Lines, Topstitches, and Puckering with more freedom. Location Main Menu Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar Edit tool for the respective item Note: Edit Tools for Respective Items Pattern Transform Pattern (A) Line/Point Edit Pattern (Z) Sewing Edit Sewing (B) Topstitches Edit Topstitch (J) Buttons/Buttonholes Select/Move Button ([) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Edit tool for the respective item 3D/ 2D Toolbar Edit tool for the respective item Double click in the 2D window, then drag the mouse. A selection point appears where the mouse is double clicked and a line follows as the mouse is dragged. The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) Click around the items to create the lasso selection. Click on the start point to complete the lasso selection. All items related to the Edit tool are selected and highlighted in yellow. Note: Only items related to the activated Edit tool are selected. For example, if the Edit Pattern tool is used to create a polygon lasso selection, only segments and points within the lasso selection are selected.

Title: Select/Move Point/Segment
Content: Objective Modify Patterns and Internal Shapes by moving points and segments. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Select Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Click a point or segment of a Pattern or Internal Shape. The point or segment is selected. When there are multiple points or segments, a pop-up menu appears allowing you to select the desired one (ver3.0.0.) To select multiple points and segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard when clicking them. All clicked points and segments are selected. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass points and segments to be selected with the marquee box. All points and segments inside the marquee box are selected. The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar TEdit Pattern Click and drag the Pattern or use the arrow keys. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the point or segment. The point or segment can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the point or segment to type in distance moved. Option Description Distance Moved Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. X-Axis (ver4.2.0) Type in how much a point is moved on x-axis. This option does not appear for segments. Y-Axis (ver4.2.0) Type in how much a point is moved on Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. Note: If it is cumbersome to select Patterns using the Edit Pattern tool, use the Transform Pattern tool.

Title: Delete
Content: Objective Delete points, lines, Internal Shapes, and Patterns. Location Delete Point/Line Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Delete Pattern Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern Operation Delete Point/Line Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the item to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. The selected item is deleted. Delete Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern Right click on the item to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. The selected item is deleted.

Title: Select/Move/Transform Pattern
Content: Objective Select Patterns to move, transform and rotate. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Operation Select Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Click the Pattern. The Pattern is selected and highlighted in yellow. To select multiple Patterns, hold down the Shift on the keyboard and click Patterns to be selected. All clicked Patterns are now selected. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass all Patterns to be selected with a marquee box. All Patterns inside the marquee box are selected. The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Click and drag the Pattern to be moved or use the arrow keys on keyboard. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the Pattern. The Pattern can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the Pattern to type in distance moved. Transform Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Select the Pattern to be transformed and click and drag desired point of the marquee box. The selected Pattern is enlarged or shrunken. Rotate Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Select the Pattern to be rotated. Select the Rotation Point, the single point above the marquee box, and drag left or right. When the pivot point, the point at the center of the Pattern, is deactivated (in white,) the Pattern is rotated based on the center of the Pattern. Note: To select point or segment, use the Edit Pattern tool or the Transform Point/Segment tool. Double click the pivot point to activate and transform or rotate based on the pivot point.

Title: Add Perpendicular Internal Line
Content: Objective Create Internal Lines perpendicular to Pattern outlines or 2D window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Add from a Point Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the point of a Pattern outline or Internal Line. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Hover the mouse over the Add Perpendicular Internal Line option. Below options appear. X-Axis Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's X-axis. Y-Axis Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's Y-axis. Local Can type in Internal Line's angle based on the selected segment. Select the desired option. The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window with different options appears based on your selection. Option Description X-Axis/ Y-Axis Local (Pattern outline) Local (Internal Line) Angle Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length Type in Internal Line's length. Extend When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Opposite Segment Not Applicable Internal Line is created based on the other side of the selected line. Reverse Not Applicable The Internal Line is reversed. Add from a Segment Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the Pattern outline or Internal Line. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Add Perpendicular Internal Line. The Internal Line preview appears at the center of the selected Pattern outline or Internal Line. The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. Configure below options as needed and click OK. Option Description Angle Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length Type in the length of the Internal Line. Distance to Segment Edge Locate the Internal Line. The Internal Line preview shifts as number changes. Extend When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Reverse The Internal Line is reversed. The Internal Line is created accordingly.

Title: Invert Selection
Content: Objective Invert the Pattern selection, selecting the Patterns currently not selected. Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) Invert Selection Main Menu Edit Invert Selection Operation Select Patterns that will be deselected. Follow the indicated guideline as below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) Invert Selection Main Menu Edit Invert Selection All Patterns that were selected are deselected, while the remaining patterns are selected.

Title: Create Smooth Curve
Content: Objective Modify Pattern outlines or Internal Lines into smooth curves. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar Smooth Curve Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar Smooth Curve Click on a segment or point to establish the first point. The point appears in grey. Drag the mouse. A grey arrow extending from the point follows the cursor. Click on another segment or point to establish the endpoint. A reference line is created between the two points. With the reference line created, click on the side that will be converted into a smooth curve. The entire side is highlighted in yellow. Click &amp drag the reference line to create the desired smooth curve. The entire outline of the selected side is replaced by the reference line. Note: Cancel Actions Cancel All Actions While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Esc or Ctrl+Z on the keyboard and all actions are undone. Cancel Last Action While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Delete or Backspace on the keyboard and the last action is undone.

Title: Create 2D Measurements
Content: Internal Shape Objective View the position of Internal Shapes from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). Location Property Editor 2D Measurements To Outline/To Center Operation 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Tool Select the Internal Shape/Dart. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor 2D Measurements To Outline/To Center Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. To Outline View the 2D Measurements from the left, right, top, and bottom of the Internal Shape to the Pattern outline. To Center View the 2D Measurements from the center of the Internal Shape to the left, right, top, and bottom of the Pattern outline. 2D Measurements appear based on the selected items. Internal Line Objective View the position of Internal Lines or segments of Internal Shapes from the Pattern outline with 2D Measurements (ver2.5.0). Location Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Operation 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Tool Select the Internal Shape/Dart. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor 2D Measurements To Outline/To Center Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. 2D Measurements appear based on the selected items. Internal Point Objective View the position of internal points or internal curve points from the Pattern outline with 2D Measurements (ver2.5.0). Location Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Operation 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Tool Select the Internal Shape/Dart. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor 2D Measurements To Outline/To Center Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. 2D Measurements appear based on the selected items.

Title: Slash & Spread
Content: Objective Slash and spread a Pattern using an Internal Line inside the Pattern (ver2.4.0). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Slash &amp Spread 2D Toolbar Slash &amp Spread Operation Slash &amp Spread Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Slash &amp Spread 2D Toolbar Slash &amp Spread Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, Click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). Choose the side of the Pattern to be rotated. The selected side of the Pattern is highlighted in yellow. Drag the mouse cursor towards the Pattern should be rotated. The preview of the edited pattern appears. When the desired shape is achieved, click on the 2D window to complete Slash &amp Spread. Slash &amp Spread with Distance and Angle Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Slash &amp Spread 2D Toolbar Slash &amp Spread Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). Right click on the 2D window to access the pop-up menu. The Spread window appears. Enter the desired values for Distance and Angle. Distance Set how much in length the selected side of the Pattern spreads. Angle Set the angle the selected side of the Pattern spreads. Click OK to complete Slash &amp Spread. Note: When selecting an Internal Line as a Slash Line, the side closer to the mouse cursor spreads. Click on the slash line to spread patterns on both sides. (ver MD10) The shape of the Pattern can be previewed when closing the Pattern. Also, the Pattern Outline is smoothened into a natural curve. (ver MD10)

Title: Trim Style Window (Ver. 2024.1)
Content: Objective Manage Trims as a shape or style in the Trim Window. It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in Trim list window. Location Main Menu Window Trim Window Dropdown Menu Trim Operation Add &amp Apply one or more Trim Styles 1. Click Add at the top right to load a file to use as Trim. or Main Menu File Import and import a file. In the popup window, chose Object Type as Trim. or Drag and drop a file (from Library or File Explorer) directly to the Trim Style Window. A Trim style is added. 2. Drag the style from the Trim window to the 3D window, apply it and Glue. Copy &amp Paste 1. Select the added Trim style and click Copy button. The selected Trim style is copied. 2. Click the Delete button on the right side of the Trim style that is not applied to the 3D window. The selected Trim style is deleted. Change Trim Styles 1. Use Select/Move tool, to select a trim in 3D window. 2. Click the Assign button to the right of the trim style name. or Drag and drop a Trim style onto the trim you've selected. The selected Trim's style has been changed. Trim Window Add Allows you to import files to use as trims into the Trim Window. Supported file formats include .TRM, .OBJ, .FBX, .USD Copy Makes a copy of the the highlighted/selected Trim file Assign Apply or replace trim shapes/styles onto existing trims as desired. Delete Unused Removes from the Trim window any unused Trim files. Note: The default file format for Trim in Marvelous Designer is .TRM file. Other supported file formats for importing Object Types as trim include .OBJ, .FBX, and .USD.

Title: OBJ Trim Properties
Content: Objective When an OBJ is imported as a Garment, input weight and reflect it in the Simulation. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern [ Z ] / Transform Pattern [ A ] 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern Operation Select the tool/ menu indicated. Select the loaded OBJ trim. The OBJ properties are displayed in Property Editor. Modify the properties according to the following. Information Name Enter a name and an item number of the trim. Specification Scale Scale trim with X, Y, and Z-axis. Weight Set the weight of trim. The entered value of weight is reflected in the simulation. Collision (Ver. 11) Set whether you turn the Collision on or off. It only enables or disables the Collision of detached trim. Collision Thickness Set the Collision Thickness with a garment. The higher the value is, the farther the distance with a garment is in the simulation. Material Set the Material of trim. Polygon Optimization (ver. 2024.1) Count Set the number of polygons. Plane This is applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation.

Title: OBJ TRIM: Transform OBJ Trims
Content: Objective Transform OBJ files loaded as trim as needed. Location Via the Scale Gizmo Load OBJ as Trim Scale Via the Property Editor Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Via the Scale Gizmo Load an OBJ. Follow the indicated guideline below: Load OBJ as Trim Scale Click and drag on the x,y, or z-axis to transform the OBJ. Axis Description X-Axis The red axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the x-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. Y-Axis The yellow-green axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the y-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. Z-Axis The blue axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the z-axis to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. Square The yellow square located in the center of the Scale Gizmo. Click and drag the square to transform the OBJ trim, while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. The OBJ is transformed. When the OBJ transformation is complete, click the Scale button again. The Gizmo used for moving and rotating OBJs appears. Via the Property Editor Load an OBJ. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select the OBJ to be transformed. The properties of the OBJ appear in the Property Editor. Find the Scale option. Enter the desired value for the below options. Option Description X-Axis Enter the desired x-axis value. Y-Axis Enter the desired y-axis value. Z-Axis Enter the desired z-axis value. Maintain Ratio Toggle this option on to adjust an OBJ while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio.

Title: OBJ TRIM: Glue OBJ Trim
Content: Objective Glue 3D Trims onto Garments and simulate together (ver3.0.0). Location Main Menu File Import OBJ Operation Glue OBJ Trim Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Import OBJ Open File window appears. Select desired OBJ file and click OK to load. In the pop-up menu, select Load as Trim for the Object Type, and click OK. Click the loaded OBJ with the Select/Move tool. Gizmo for the selected OBJ appears. Click on the Glue icon next to the OBJ Gizmo, then mouse over the desired location. OBJ preview tags along the mouse. Click on the desired location. Selected OBJ automatically attaches to the place. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and angle. Note: To cancel the arrangement, press Esc on the keyboard. Activate Simulation. OBJ is now being simulated along with the rest of the Garments. Note: You can select multiple OBJ trims and move or rotate those by using Gizmo. (ver. 11 ) Delete OBJ Trim Right click on the OBJ trim. OBJ is now being selected and a pop-up menu appears. Note: Relevant menu above does not appear for OBJ trims that are not glued to the Garments. Click on Delete to remove it. Selected OBJ is now being removed from the Garments.

Title: OBJ TRIM: Copy/Paste Trims
Content: Objective Copy and paste trims in the 3D window. Location Copy Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Copy Paste Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Paste Operation Load an OBJ as a Trim. Select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. To copy a trim, follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Copy The selected trim is copied. To paste the copied trim, follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Paste Click to place the duplicated trim in the 3D window. The trim is pasted. Note: To copy and paste multiple trims, hold down Shift on the keyboard and select all trims to be copied, then perform the procedure above. When copying and pasting multiple trims, they must all be placed within a Pattern. Shortcuts for copy and paste are Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V respectively.

Title: OBJ TRIM: Set OBJ Trim Weight
Content: Objective When an OBJ is imported as a Garment, input weight and reflect in the Simulation. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move(Q) 3D Toolbar Select/Move(Q) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Select the loaded OBJ trim. The OBJ properties display in Property Editor. Enter desired value at Simulation Properties Weight, and simulate. The value is now being applied and simulated accordingly.

Title: Avatar Measure (above ver 10)
Content: Objective Measure the circumference, length and height of the Avatar. Two methods are provided. Either based on the protruding part of the avatar or based on the surface of the curvature. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement 3D Toolbar Click and hold down the Basic Circumference Measure Operation Basic/Surface Circumference Measure. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the starting point to be measured and click the second point in the desired direction. A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is displayed. Click once more when it is in the target shape. A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is created and the length is displayed. Basic/Surface/Linear Measure Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the start point to be measured and double-click the end point. A Basic/Surface/Linear Tape Measure is created and its length is displayed. A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. Height Measure Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the point to be measured. A Height Measure that runs vertically from the clicked point to the ground is created and the length is displayed. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create vertical/horizontal/45 tilt. Use Attach to Measure tool to attach the pattern outline or Internal Line to the Avatar Measure. Attach to Measure (Avatar) Objective Attach avatar tapes to internal or external seam/pattern lines. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement Attach to Measure (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Click and hold down the Edit Measure (Avatar) Attach to Measure (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: In the 3D window, select seam or pattern line to attach to avatar tape. Pattern with the selected line becomes transparent and the selected line gets highlighted in red. Select avatar tape to be attached. Once it is selected, the pattern becomes normal, the attached seam or pattern line and the avatar tape becomes in red. To detach avatar tape from seam or pattern line, click on Attach to Avatar Tape tool again, and press 'Delete' on keyboard. Edit Measure (Avatar) Option Objective Show or hide the length indicated on the Tape Measure Location 3D Toolbar Edit Measure (Avatar) Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the Tape Measure and set the options below. Delete Measure Delete the Tape Measure Duplicate to Symmetric Position (ver 11) Duplicate the tape measure to the symmetrical position of the avatar. Show/ Show All Length The selected tape measure or the length of the entire tape measure is shown or hidden.

Title: Attach to Avatar Tape  (ver. 5.1.4)
Content: Related articles Linear Avatar Tape Circumference Avatar Tape Delete Avatar Tape Objective Attach avatar tapes to internal or external seam/pattern lines. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Attach to Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Attach to Avatar Tape Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Attach to Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Attach to Avatar Tape In the 3D window, select a seam or pattern line to attach to avatar tape. Pattern with the selected line becomes transparent and the selected line gets highlighted in red. Select avatar tape to be attached. Once it is selected, the pattern becomes normal, and the attached seam or pattern line and the avatar tape become red. To detach avatar tape from the seam or pattern line, click on Attach to Avatar Tape tool again, and press 'Delete' on the keyboard.

Title: Linear Avatar Tape  (ver. 5.1.4)
Content: Related articles Circumference Avatar Tape Attach to Avatar Tape Delete Avatar Tape Objective Create a linear baseline to improve accuracy in fit and draping on the 3D window. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Linear Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Linear Avatar Tape Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Linear Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Linear Avatar Tape Click to make the beginning point of the tape at a desired place. Blue dot appears and gets fixed. Note: Pressing the Shift key on the keyboard before creating the beginning point provides a guideline on the avatar. Click another place to make the second point. Another blue dot appears and gets fixed and a connected line between both of the dots appears. Double-click to complete.
